html:
The Anggamudi were an Aboriginal Australian people of the far north of the Cape York Peninsula, near its western side. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Little is recorded of them. The tip of Cape York was home to many small peoples, each with its own speech, and the Anggamudi were one of them. Neighbours on the map include the Wuthathi, the Anguthimri and the Lotiga. Across Torres Strait to the north lived the island peoples who traded with both Cape York and New Guinea. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
